claims.explanation: Bergenin's anti-inflammatory activity is mediated by inhibiting NF-kB and MAPK signaling and by suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-alpha and IL-1beta, which are annotated targets. Cancer cell lines that depend on constitutive NF-kB/cytokine signaling (e.g., high IL1B/TNF expression or NF-kB pathway activation) should be more sensitive, while lines with low inflammatory tone or intact antioxidant/Nrf2 responses may be protected. The virtual-cell profile showing downregulation of TNIP1 (an NF-kB inhibitor) and upregulation of IKBKE (an NF-kB activator) is consistent with perturbation of NF-kB signaling as the selective mechanism.
